items.title: AB-3028 Programmable T Cell Therapy for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This early-stage trial is testing AB-3028, a new type of immune cell therapy that is programmed to target metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is currently recruiting patients and will evaluate both safety and how well the treatment works. This is a phase 1/2 trial, meaning it is still in early testing stages.

items.title: Niraparib Plus Abiraterone for Metastatic Prostate Cancer Phase 3
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether adding niraparib (a PARP inhibitor) to standard abiraterone treatment improves outcomes in metastatic prostate cancer. The study is no longer recruiting new patients but is still ongoing. PARP inhibitors work by blocking cancer cells' ability to repair DNA damage.

items.title: Pasritamig With Docetaxel Versus Docetaxel Alone Phase 3
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares pasritamig combined with docetaxel chemotherapy to docetaxel alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is currently recruiting and aims to see if the combination delays disease progression on imaging scans. Pasritamig is a targeted therapy directed at cancer cells.

items.title: Mevrometostat for Castration Resistant Prostate Cancer Phase 1
items.summary: This trial studies mevrometostat, a drug that targets a specific enzyme involved in cancer growth, for patients with castration-resistant prostate cancer who have progressed after previous treatments. Part 3 is currently recruiting and will test mevrometostat alone or combined with enzalutamide. This is an early-stage phase 1 trial.

items.title: Pasritamig Versus Placebo Phase 3 Late-Line mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial evaluates whether pasritamig combined with best supportive care improves overall survival compared to placebo in late-stage metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have already received multiple treatments. The trial is currently recruiting patients. This represents a potential option for heavily pre-treated patients.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Phase 3 for Metastatic Hormone-Sensitive
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether adding mevrometostat to enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer who have not yet received hormone therapy. The study is currently recruiting. This is for earlier-stage metastatic disease before castration resistance develops.

items.title: Cabozantinib and Atezolizumab for Metastatic CRPC Phase 2
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether the combination of cabozantinib (which blocks enzymes needed for tumor growth) and atezolizumab (an immunotherapy) can shrink tumors in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The trial is currently recruiting patients. This combines two different treatment approaches.

items.title: Pasritamig in Combination With Other Agents Phase 1
items.summary: This early-stage trial is testing pasritamig combined with various other treatments for metastatic prostate cancer. The study is currently recruiting and aims to find the best dose and combination approach. Phase 1 trials focus on safety and determining optimal dosing.

items.title: Radium-223 Plus M3814 Plus Avelumab for Advanced CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests radium-223 (radioactive treatment) alone, combined with M3814 (a drug that blocks DNA repair), or with both M3814 and avelumab (immunotherapy) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is recruiting and aims to find the best combination approach. Radium-223 delivers radiation directly to bone metastases.

items.title: Mevrometostat Plus Enzalutamide Phase 3 for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether mevrometostat combined with enzalutamide works better than enzalutamide alone in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients who have not previously received enzalutamide or abiraterone. The study is currently recruiting. This targets patients earlier in their treatment journey.

items.title: Sacituzumab Govitecan After AR-Directed Therapy Phase 2
items.summary: This phase 2 study investigates sacituzumab govitecan (an antibody-drug conjugate) in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer patients whose disease has progressed on newer hormone therapies like enzalutamide or abiraterone. The trial is no longer recruiting but is still active. This drug delivers chemotherapy directly to cancer cells.

items.title: INV-9956 Safety and Activity Study for Advanced mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates the safety, how the body processes the drug, and anti-tumor activity of INV-9956 in advanced metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study is currently recruiting patients. Early-stage trials help determine if a new drug is safe and shows promise.

items.title: Duration of Hormone Therapy With Radiation for Oligometastatic Prostate
items.summary: This phase 2 trial studies whether adding abiraterone to standard radiation and hormone therapy improves quality of life in oligometastatic prostate cancer (cancer spread to only a few sites). The study is currently recruiting. Treatment duration and intensity are key questions being addressed.

items.title: Ferroptosis and Prostate Cancer Treatment Mechanisms Review
items.summary: This research review discusses ferroptosis, a type of programmed cell death, as a potential treatment approach for castration-resistant prostate cancer. The paper summarizes how triggering ferroptosis could help overcome drug resistance and work synergistically with current therapies. This is translational research connecting laboratory findings to potential clinical applications.

items.title: Nanocatalytic Therapy for Overcoming Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers developed an injectable treatment that delivers nanoparticles and chloroquine to fight castration-resistant prostate cancer. The nanoparticles generate reactive oxygen species to damage cancer cells while chloroquine blocks the cells' repair mechanisms. This is preclinical research showing promise in laboratory models.

items.title: CDK4/6 Inhibitor Dalpiciclib Enhances Enzalutamide in CRPC Models
items.summary: This preclinical study found that combining the CDK4/6 inhibitor dalpiciclib with enzalutamide showed strong anti-tumor activity in castration-resistant prostate cancer models. The combination works by blocking DNA replication in cancer cells. This is laboratory research that could lead to future clinical trials.

items.title: Real-World Comparison of Enzalutamide and Apalutamide in mHSPC
items.summary: This real-world study compared enzalutamide and apalutamide in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer patients in Japan. Both drugs showed similar effectiveness in PSA response, time to castration resistance, and overall survival. This provides practical evidence about two commonly used treatments.

items.title: USP2 Protein Facilitates Therapy Resistance in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: Researchers identified USP2, a protein that increases when prostate cancer becomes resistant to hormone therapies and chemotherapy. USP2 helps cancer cells survive by stabilizing proteins that promote cancer growth. Understanding this mechanism could lead to new treatment strategies to overcome resistance.

items.title: Bavdegalutamide Plus Abiraterone Phase 1b Trial Results
items.source: Clinical cancer research : an official journal of the American Association for Cancer Research
items.summary: This phase 1b trial tested bavdegalutamide (ARV-110), a PROTAC drug that degrades the androgen receptor, combined with abiraterone in metastatic prostate cancer patients progressing on abiraterone. The combination was well-tolerated with promising PSA responses. This represents a novel mechanism to overcome hormone therapy resistance.

items.title: Radiopharmaceutical Therapy Advances for Prostate Cancer Review
items.summary: This review summarizes major 2025 advances in radiopharmaceutical therapy for prostate cancer. The field has evolved from radium-223 for bone metastases to PSMA-targeted therapies that can treat various metastatic sites. These treatments deliver radiation directly to cancer cells throughout the body.

items.title: Terbium-161-PSMA After Lutetium-177-PSMA Progression Study
items.summary: This study evaluated [161Tb]Tb-PSMA-617 in 15 mCRPC patients who had progressed after [177Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 treatment. Terbium-161 emits different types of radiation that may be more effective. This explores whether switching to a different radioisotope can help after progression on lutetium-177.

items.title: Combined Radium-223 and Lutetium-177-PSMA in Advanced mCRPC
items.summary: This case report describes a patient with advanced mCRPC treated with combined radium-223 and lutetium-177-PSMA therapy. The combination was well-tolerated initially with favorable response, though the patient eventually progressed. This illustrates the feasibility of combining two different radioactive treatments.

items.title: Actinium-225 More Effective Than Lutetium-177 in Prostate Models
items.source: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
items.summary: This preclinical study compared actinium-225 (an alpha-emitter) to lutetium-177 (a beta-emitter) attached to NM600 in prostate cancer models. Actinium-225 showed superior anti-tumor effects. Alpha-emitting radiopharmaceuticals deliver more concentrated radiation over shorter distances, potentially increasing effectiveness.

items.title: Radium-223 After Lutetium-177-PSMA Safety and Efficacy Study
items.summary: This multi-center study analyzed 21 mCRPC patients who received radium-223 after progressing on lutetium-177-PSMA. Only 19% completed all planned treatments, with common reasons for stopping being disease progression and blood count toxicity. This provides important safety data about treatment sequencing.
